excerpt: Magic Eden is a Solana NFT marketplace valued at $1.6 billion in 2022. In 2026 it closed its Bitcoin and EVM markets and wallet to focus on Solana and gaming.
content:
Magic Eden is a marketplace for buying, selling and minting NFTs. It started on the Solana blockchain in 2021 and grew quickly, later adding Polygon and other EVM chains and a Bitcoin Ordinals marketplace, letting buyers pay by credit card, and launching a multi-chain crypto wallet. In December 2024 it launched its own token, ME, with a large airdrop to users.

Jack Lu is cofounder and CEO. In June 2022, nine months after launch, Magic Eden raised a $130 million Series B co-led by Electric Capital and Greylock at a $1.6 billion valuation, with Lightspeed, Paradigm and Sequoia also investing, TechCrunch reported; that came three months after a $27 million Series A. As NFT trading fell, it cut 22 jobs, about 15% of staff, in February 2023, The Block reported. In February 2026 Lu said Magic Eden would shut its EVM and Bitcoin NFT marketplaces in March, its Bitcoin API later that month and its wallet on 1 April, because, he said, 80% of costs went to products bringing in 20% of revenue. Cointelegraph and Crypto Briefing reported that it would focus on Solana, NFT packs and Dicey, a crypto casino and sports betting product.

Using Magic Eden's marketplace is free to browse; trades carry marketplace and creator fees set by Magic Eden and each collection, shown before you buy. NFTs and crypto tokens are volatile and can lose most of their value, and online gambling products carry their own risks and legal limits.

We have not used Magic Eden for this page. It brings together Magic Eden's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
